title: Rating Note: How a Keyturn Trip Booking Reservation Is Priced and What Lines It Raises
content:
A Keyturn Trip Booking reservation is priced from the daily rate the host had published at the moment the reservation was confirmed, never the price showing today, and that locked rate is the basis of every later line raised on the reservation.

**Base rate.** The base rate is the locked daily rate multiplied by the reserved days, where reserved days are the reserved hours divided by twenty-four and rounded up to the next whole day, with a floor of one day. Reservations running a week or more take the plan's weekly discount off the base rate, and reservations running a month or more take the monthly discount instead of the weekly one rather than on top of it.

**Marketplace trip fee.** The marketplace trip fee is a percentage of the discounted base rate and is never lower than the plan's trip fee floor; where the percentage yields less than the floor, the floor is charged.

**Young-driver line.** Where the driver is under the young-driver threshold on the first day of the reserved period, the young-driver surcharge is posted as its own line, so that it can be reversed on its own if the driver's age is later corrected. The basis on which that surcharge was formerly computed, namely that such a driver "pays the young-driver surcharge on the discounted base rate", is **no longer in force** and must not be applied.

**Handover lines.** Delivery is charged only where the vehicle is brought to the guest, and the airport surcharge is added on top of the delivery fee when the delivery point is an airport; where the guest collects the vehicle themselves neither line is raised, and a line that is not raised is not the same as a line raised at zero.

**Deposit.** A refundable deposit is authorised at confirmation unless the guest's driver score reaches the plan's waiver score, in which case no deposit line is raised at all; where a deposit is taken it is released after the plan's hold period counted from the day the trip ends.

**Line identity.** Every line carries the basis it was priced on, so that two lines posted on the same day for the same reservation are always separable, and a line is posted only while the reservation is in the requested, booked or in-progress state.

### The reserved days and the discount, worked through

*Hypothetical inputs: a reserved period of 200 reserved hours on a plan whose weekly discount is 12 per cent and whose monthly discount is 22 per cent, at a locked daily rate of 80.00 USD.*

Two hundred reserved hours divided by twenty-four is eight and one third, which rounds up to the next whole day: 9 reserved days. The floor of one day does not bite. Nine days multiplied by 80.00 USD gives an undiscounted base of 720.00 USD. The reservation runs a week or more but not a month, so the weekly discount of 12 per cent is taken off and the monthly discount is not: the discounted base rate is 633.60 USD. The two discounts never stand together on one reservation — where the reservation runs a month or more, the monthly discount is taken instead of the weekly one.

*Continuing, on a plan whose trip fee is 11.5 per cent with a floor of 4.95 USD.* Eleven and a half per cent of 633.60 USD is 72.86 USD, which is above the floor, so 72.86 USD is charged. Had the percentage yielded less than 4.95 USD, the floor of 4.95 USD would have been charged instead.

### The state gate on a priced line

A priced line is raised only while the reservation stands in the requested, booked or in-progress state, read from the reservation's own record before the line is posted and correlated to it by the reservation's reference number. The reservation's status is a system record; it is not settled on either party's account of where the trip has got to.
